Lesson 3 · Guided route

Make uncertainty part of the decision: guided case

Is the average online quote meaningfully different from the matched offline quote?

Work through 5 selected steps. The short case gives the decision first; the technical appendix holds the complete model and derivations.

Short caseTechnical appendix
Guided steps
  1. 01. A new case: compare the same products across channels
  2. 02. A small mean can hide a wide range of differences
  3. 03. Measure the mean difference in standard errors
  4. 04. A significant average difference is not a universal price claim
  5. 05. Separate the estimate, uncertainty and decision

Guided step 01 / 5

A new case: compare the same products across channels

The retail case generates 40 fictional products with an offline and online quote for each product at the same time and under the same assumed quantity and tax definition. Product base prices vary widely. Pairing uses the product, not arbitrary row order.

The analysis unit is one matched product difference. Before pairing real data, verify exact product identity, package size, currency, availability, observation time and missing matches. Preserve exclusions and the unmatched count. A shared name alone may not identify the same product.

The synthetic generator creates independent product differences, normally distributed with authored mean 0.45 and SD 1.55 CU. Product base prices create strong dependence between channels within a pair. Treating the two channel columns as independent would discard that design.

Pause and explain

What is the independent unit for the paired test in this example?

Compare your reasoning

The product-level difference. The two prices within a product are deliberately related and must remain paired.

Guided step 02 / 5

A small mean can hide a wide range of differences

Observed product differences range from -1.88 to 3.44 CU, while their mean is 0.788 CU. A mean near zero could conceal offsetting positive and negative differences. Inspect the paired difference distribution, not only the two marginal price distributions.

The plot keeps every generated product. A central zoom can be useful, but it must preserve the original sample definition and disclose what lies outside the view. Do not discard large differences simply because a zoom makes them inconvenient. Investigate whether they reflect package mismatch, promotions, timing or a genuine tail.

Product order is arbitrary here; no time trend should be inferred from left-to-right position. For a paired t procedure, normality concerns the differences, not a requirement that both original price columns be separately normal.

Pause and explain

Does a mean difference of zero imply every product has equal prices?

Compare your reasoning

No. Positive and negative product differences can cancel. The mean is one summary of the difference distribution, not an equality statement for every pair.

Guided step 03 / 5

Measure the mean difference in standard errors

A paired t test is a one-sample t test on dᵢ = onlineᵢ − offlineᵢ. Under a zero-mean null, divide the sample mean difference by its SE. With independent normally distributed differences, the statistic follows a t distribution with n − 1 degrees of freedom under the null.

t = (d̄ − 0)/(s_d/√n); paired 95% CI = d̄ ± t₀.₉₇₅,ₙ₋₁ × s_d/√n
Paired test calculated from the generated raw pairs

Pairs40

t statistic3.671424
Degrees of freedom39
Two-sided p-value0.0007213
95% CI CU0.354051 to 1.222760

The p-value compares the magnitude |t| with both tails of the null t distribution. Pairing can improve precision because stable product-level differences in price level cancel. That benefit depends on preserving correct matches and a defensible independence structure across products.

Pause and explain

What error results from pairing one product’s online quote with another product’s offline quote?

Compare your reasoning

The differences no longer represent the intended matched comparison. Both the estimand and the uncertainty calculation become misleading.

Guided step 04 / 5

A significant average difference is not a universal price claim

The paired 95% interval, 0.354 to 1.223 CU, excludes zero. Under the authored paired model, that supports a nonzero average channel difference. It does not say every online quote is higher, that the gap is important, or that switching channels causes this difference in a real population.

An interval makes the magnitude visible. Compare its range with a decision-relevant tolerance established before inspecting results. Also separate uncertainty about the population average from variability across individual products. A narrow mean interval can coexist with large positive and negative individual differences.

For a real operational recommendation, consider transaction fees, travel or delivery costs, availability, timing and the relevant product mix. These can dominate a small average quote difference. The synthetic exercise deliberately excludes those complications so the statistical distinction stays visible.

Pause and explain

Can a statistically detectable difference still be too small to matter operationally?

Compare your reasoning

Yes. A test against exactly zero can reject even when the plausible mean differences all lie within a prespecified practically negligible range.

Guided step 05 / 5

Separate the estimate, uncertainty and decision

A defensible inference brief names the target, observation unit, design, exclusions, estimator and uncertainty method. It distinguishes the statistical result from the operational recommendation and states the assumptions most likely to change the conclusion.

Choose an inferential method from the claim and design
QuestionMethod and caution
One population meant interval when justified; check IID and distribution
One probabilityBinomial/Wilson methods; define event and dependence
Matched comparisonAnalyze differences; preserve pair identity
Independent meansWelch method; do not invent pairing
Practical equivalencePrespecified margin and TOST, not a failed zero test
Many questionsDefine the family and control the relevant error target

Example handoff: “For 40 independently generated matched products, online minus offline averages 0.788 CU (95% CI 0.354 to 1.223). The mean is detectably nonzero and also falls within a prespecified ±1.50 CU equivalence margin under TOST. This concerns an average in an authored synthetic model, not all products or real retailers.”

Before acting, ask four questions: Is the target clear? Does the design support it? Is the uncertainty method matched to the estimator and dependence? Would the plausible effect change the decision? Continue to regression with those questions intact.

Pause and explain

What makes a statistically correct computation an incomplete recommendation?

Compare your reasoning

A missing target population, unsupported design assumption, unexamined practical consequence or hidden analysis search can make the computation irrelevant to the decision even when its arithmetic is correct.

Compare with the known truth

Reveal the generator truth

The paired-difference generator sets the population mean to 0.45 CU. The observed average differs because this is one random sample. The other cases in this lesson have separate generators and targets.

This comparison is possible because the case is synthetic. The full generating process is in the appendix.
